sections.title: Commercial Real Estate Analytics
sections.description: For CBRE Chicago, JLL Chicago, and the institutional commercial real estate investors.

blocks.heading: Chicago office market analytics
paragraphs: ML for Chicago's large office market — demand prediction incorporating downtown Chicago's specific submarkets (Loop, River North, West Loop, Fulton Market), the tech company presence effect on Fulton Market and the West Loop, and the return-to-office dynamics affecting Chicago's large financial and professional services employer community.

blocks.heading: Industrial and logistics real estate ML
paragraphs: ML for Chicago's enormous industrial market — the supply and demand analytics for the large distribution centers, logistics facilities, and manufacturing properties that Chicago's central US geography and rail hub create. Chicago's industrial market is among the US's most active, driven by e-commerce fulfillment and supply chain reshoring.

blocks.heading: Retail real estate analytics
paragraphs: ML for the large retail REIT portfolios managed from Chicago — predicting tenant survival, lease renewal probability, and rent growth for the suburban Chicago retail centers managed by Inland Real Estate and the other Chicago-area retail property companies.

sections.title: Residential AVM (Automated Valuation Models)
sections.description: For the residential real estate market serving Chicago's diverse neighborhoods.

blocks.heading: Cook County property AVM
paragraphs: ML for Cook County's large residential assessment program — the Cook County Assessor's Office has used open-source AI tools developed by the University of Chicago's Center for Data Science and Public Policy to create an AVM that is now a national model for government property assessment fairness. Commercial AI for residential brokers and lenders operating in Cook County must account for the specific property characteristics and neighborhood dynamics that the Assessor's AVM captures.

blocks.heading: Chicago neighborhood-level residential ML
paragraphs: ML calibrated to Chicago's extreme neighborhood-level real estate variation — the price per square foot in Lincoln Park and in Englewood differs by 10x, and suburban Cook County's market differs from the city's in ways that regional AVM models underrepresent.

sections.title: Equity Residential Portfolio Analytics
sections.description: For Equity Residential (Chicago HQ) — the third-largest US apartment REIT.

blocks.heading: Multi-family demand forecasting
paragraphs: ML for Equity Residential's large apartment portfolio across multiple US markets — predicting occupancy, renewal probability, and rent growth across EQR's 80,000+ units in Boston, New York, Washington DC, Seattle, San Francisco, and Southern California.

blocks.heading: Resident experience and retention ML
paragraphs: ML for EQR's resident satisfaction and retention programs — predicting move-out probability 90+ days before lease expiration enables the proactive renewal outreach that reduces turnover cost for EQR's large portfolio.

blocks.heading: Affordable housing investment analytics
paragraphs: ML for the community development financial institutions (CDFIs) and affordable housing developers serving Chicago's underserved neighborhoods — predicting project feasibility, community impact, and long-term affordability sustainability for the Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) projects that finance affordable housing in Chicago.

blocks.heading: Neighborhood investment signal analytics
paragraphs: ML for identifying Chicago neighborhoods at the early stages of investment and potential displacement — enabling community development organizations to deploy resources before market pressure forces low-income residents out.

sections.title: Chicago real estate AI regulatory context
sections.description: Key regulatory considerations for real estate AI development in Illinois.

blocks.heading: Illinois Real Estate License Act
paragraphs: AI used in real estate brokerage in Illinois must comply with the Real Estate License Act's disclosure requirements for automated valuation tools.

blocks.heading: BIPA for any property inspection AI
paragraphs: Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act may apply to real estate AI using facial recognition for property access or showing management — ClickMasters designs all Chicago real estate AI without biometric features by default.

blocks.heading: Cook County property tax system
paragraphs: Chicago's unusually complex property tax system — Cook County uses different multipliers for different property classes and has a complex exemption structure — creates property tax analytics AI demand that is specific to the Cook County context.

sections.title: Chicago's real estate AI landscape in 2025
sections.description: Chicago's real estate market has specific dynamics driving AI investment.

blocks.heading: Cook County's open government data advantage
paragraphs: The Cook County Assessor's decision to publish its AVM methodology and model code as open source has created an unusually data-rich foundation for private sector real estate AI in Chicago. Developers can leverage the Assessor's publicly available methodology to build private applications that benefit from the government's investment in property data transparency.

blocks.heading: Chicago's industrial market AI surge
paragraphs: Chicago's industrial market — one of the US's largest and most active — has experienced an AI analytics surge driven by e-commerce fulfillment demand. The question of where to locate the next fulfillment center in the Chicago metro (which suburb, which access road, which size) has become a ML-driven optimization for the large industrial REITs and logistics companies competing for Chicago's distribution geography.

blocks.heading: Affordable housing crisis as AI driver
paragraphs: Chicago's affordable housing challenge — including the decades-long impact of historically discriminatory housing policies on the South and West Side's property values and investment levels — has made equitable housing analytics an active area of government and nonprofit AI investment. The City of Chicago's data portal provides rich datasets that support community development AI with fewer data barriers than most US cities.
